qs_063:n2.prompt:
You are helping me compare payroll providers ({{vendor}}) so I can choose one to run payroll, file employment taxes, and administer benefits for my company. Before starting, ask me for any of the following you need: my company's state(s) of operation, headcount and whether employees are full-time/part-time/contractors, whether I need benefits administration (health insurance, 401k, etc.), my current or planned HR/accounting tools (for integration needs), my budget range, and any must-have features (e.g., multi-state filing, contractor payments, time tracking).

Once you have these inputs, research and compare at least 3-5 {{vendor}} options suited to my company's size and needs. For each candidate, gather and summarize: pricing structure (base fee + per-employee cost), states/countries supported for tax filing, whether they handle federal/state/local employment tax filings automatically, benefits administration capabilities, integrations with accounting/HR tools I use, contractor payment support, customer support quality/reputation, and any notable limitations or complaints.

Organize findings into a clear comparison table (provider name, pricing, tax filing coverage, benefits support, integrations, pros/cons) so I can quickly evaluate tradeoffs. Highlight the top 2-3 candidates that best match my stated requirements, with a brief rationale for each recommendation.

Done looks like: a structured comparison document/table covering all candidates evaluated, with a shortlist of top recommendations and reasoning, ready for me to review.

Report back with the comparison table, your shortlist and reasoning, and any open questions or missing information you couldn't resolve through research. Do not sign up for, purchase, or commit to any provider — this step is preparation only, and choosing/enrolling remains a human step.

qs_063:n3.prompt:
You are helping me sign up for and configure {{vendor}}, our chosen payroll provider, to run payroll, file employment taxes, and administer benefits. If you don't already have them, ask me for: our company legal name, EIN, business address, list of employees/contractors with roles and pay rates, desired pay schedule(s) per team (weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, monthly), which states we have employees in, whether we want to offer health insurance and/or a 401(k)/retirement plan, and the {{vendor}} account login details (use your configured credentials).

Please go to {{vendor}}'s site and: create or access the company account, fill in company profile fields, configure pay schedules per team, add employee and contractor records with the information I provide, set up multi-state payroll registrations where applicable, and configure benefits administration (health insurance and/or 401(k)) so deductions and contributions will sync with payroll once active. Where {{vendor}} supports self-serve new-hire onboarding, prepare and queue invitations so new hires can submit W-4, I-9, and bank details themselves.

Do NOT enter or request the owner's SSN, bank account numbers, or any banking credentials, and do NOT sign, attest to, or submit any tax-authorization forms (e.g., EIN verification, direct deposit authorization, tax e-file authorization) — these require the owner's identity verification and signature and remain a human step. Prepare all fields you can, flag exactly which forms/screens require the owner's manual entry and signature, then stop for human sign-off.

Because this is an async/form-based signup, note that verification (e.g., bank micro-deposits, tax ID confirmation) may take time — record what to poll or check later. Report back: what was configured, what's pending {{vendor}} verification, and the exact list of items awaiting my manual entry/signature.

qs_063:n4.prompt:
You are helping me connect my payroll provider ({{vendor}}) to my accounting software so payroll journal entries sync automatically into my books. If you don't already know these, ask me for: (1) the name of {{vendor}} and confirmation I have configured credentials for it, (2) the name of my accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks, Xero, or other), and (3) whether I already have an integration or connector between the two set up.

Once you have this info, please:
1. Check whether {{vendor}} offers a native accounting integration or connector for my accounting software via its dashboard settings or integrations directory.
2. If a native integration exists, walk through the setup using my configured credentials — this typically involves authorizing {{vendor}} to connect to my accounting software account and mapping payroll categories (wages, taxes, benefits deductions) to the correct chart-of-accounts entries.
3. If no native integration exists, determine whether {{vendor}} supports exporting payroll journal data (CSV or via API) so entries can be pulled and reconciled into my ledger, and describe the steps to set that up.
4. If {{vendor}} supports webhooks for payroll lifecycle events (payroll processed, employee onboarded, payment failed), check whether these are relevant to automating the accounting sync, and note how to subscribe to them if useful.
5. Confirm the mapping is correct by identifying where a test or sample payroll journal entry would post in the accounting software.

Done looks like: the payroll-to-accounting connection is either fully configured and validated (journal entries flow into the correct ledger accounts), or — if the setup requires me to authorize a financial data connection or accept terms — you have everything prepared and ready and you stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: what integration method was used or recommended, the account mapping details, whether webhooks were configured, and any remaining manual steps I need to complete.
